### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **12** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **4** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/data.json`, `packages/spec/export-origins/data.json`, `packages/spec/src/data/external-binding-datasource.ts`, …), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**20** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 284e04810a309d5a7c8c3654b036f9ebf07a53d4`.

⛔ **9** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **4** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/data.json`, `packages/spec/export-origins/data.json`, `packages/spec/src/data/external-binding-datasource.ts`, …) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **3** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **145** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 284e04810a309d5a7c8c3654b036f9ebf07a53d4` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `f91841b75c994dcb3d64b84f7456c78fcd5cae02` — the merge of head `18e6e72566f3f68afebb2b3d9b868c3aeb15400a` into base `284e04810a309d5a7c8c3654b036f9ebf07a53d4`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin f91841b75c994dcb3d64b84f7456c78fcd5cae02 && git checkout f91841b75c994dcb3d64b84f7456c78fcd5cae02
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 284e04810a309d5a7c8c3654b036f9ebf07a53d4 18e6e72566f3f68afebb2b3d9b868c3aeb15400a && git checkout -B drift-repro 284e04810a309d5a7c8c3654b036f9ebf07a53d4 && git merge --no-ff 18e6e72566f3f68afebb2b3d9b868c3aeb15400a

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 284e04810a309d5a7c8c3654b036f9ebf07a53d4
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 284e04810a309d5a7c8c3654b036f9ebf07a53d4` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `4f2cf2423d84c348f6bccd4194f739fa690a1841`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/data/external-binding-datasource.ts, packages/spec/src/data/index.ts, packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.object-external-binding-managed-datasource-refused.ts, packages/spec/src/stack.zod.ts + packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts, packages/spec/api-surface/data.json, packages/spec/export-origins/data.json, .changeset/25211-external-binding-save-doors.md, .changeset/25168-external-binding-managed-datasource-refused.md, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.external-binding-named-datasource-refusal.test.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.external-binding-primary-datasource-refusal.test.ts, packages/spec/src/stack-external-binding-datasource.test.ts, packages/rest/src/meta-item-write-routes.ts, packages/rest/src/meta-item-history-routes.ts, packages/services/service-datasource/src/datasource-admin-service.ts, packages/services/service-datasource/src/datasource-admin-plugin.ts, packages/spec/src/data/datasource.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/shared/strict-object.ts, packages/spec/src/conversions/refused-shapes.ts, packages/objectql/src/registry.ts, scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs, scripts/check-adr-0087-registration.mjs, content/docs/data-modeling/external-datasources.mdx, scripts/engine-double-contract.pinned.json

Inputs: card #25211 (body, triage 6342661544, claim 6344231813, dev report 6347635039); #25168 (body, its dev report 6339972223 and the rest of its thread), PR #25192 (body, file list, its changeset and semantic entry as merged at `fe0ec2bb9e`) and the contract review 6340232647 on it; the domain:spec declaration 6346165242 on #18549; PR #25257's body with its Acceptance notes, its 13-file list, and the net diff of `4f2cf2423d` against its merge base with `main`, `e3190b9494`; the 42 check-runs on this head: 36 success, 6 skipped by path selection (18.x upgrade harness, Console Pin Gate, the Dogfood shards, Dogfood Verify CLI, Packed-tarball smoke, Temporal Conformance), 0 failed, 0 pending. The five required contexts (Lint & Repo Gates, TypeScript Type Check, Test Core, Build Core, Governed Surface Queue Guard) are success, and so are Check Changeset (the job that runs `check-adr-0087-registration`), Lint · PM dispatch-gates, Spec property liveness, Dogfood Regression Gate (aggregate; its shards path-skipped, so the dev's `dogfood_battery` line, pinned to this full sha, 288 files and 2411 tests with no failures, is the dogfood reading) and the three card/branch guards. The Check Changeset job's log text could not be downloaded (the log endpoint answered Forbidden); its conclusion stands as the verdict. Nothing built, run or re-run locally; every committed blob was read with `git show` after a fetch into a ref this session owns. Not read: the dispatch order and the seat's conclusions.

Face: schema. The four `packages/spec/src/**` hits above decide the tier; the PR body and the changeset also carry `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` line-initially, which `record-recognisers` reads as the narrowing face too (`yes (narrowing)` included, by its own docblock), so `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` stands on either reading.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **One predicate, no second copy — RIGHT.** `packages/spec/src/data/external-binding-datasource.ts` changes in its docblock only (every hunk sits inside the leading comment); the rule, the two message texts and the signature are byte-identical to `8a978cd3`. Both save-door halves call it: the object half with the body's `external`, its `datasource` and the definition `readMetaItem` resolves; the datasource half once per bound object with the saved body as `declared`, keeping only `shape === 'managed'` findings (a selection on the predicate's own result, not a second rule: the `primary` shape is a fact about the object alone and is refused by the object's own parse). `composeStacks` reuses `defineStack`'s `collectExternalBindingDatasourceErrors`, which calls the same predicate, over step 2's merged objects and every input's `datasources`. `packages/objectql` is untouched.

2. **The accept set of `saveMetaItem` narrows — RIGHT, and every write path through it reaches the refusal exactly once.** The block (protocol.ts, after `defaultRecordPageSaveRefusal`) reads neither `request.mode` nor `request.force`: it runs for draft and publish saves alike, after the per-type Zod gate (so the body is its declared type and the `'default'` half is already judged) and before the authoring gate and every write. `force` is read only by the destructive-diff gate for objects, a separate block; the test pins `force: true` refused. Callers measured on the head: `PUT /api/v1/meta/TYPE/NAME` (`meta-item-write-routes.ts:364`, `force` forwarded); `publishMetaItem` (`meta-item-history-routes.ts:714`) and each item of `publishPackageDrafts` promote through `promoteDraftForPublish`, which re-asks the predicate on the draft body before `repo.promoteDraft` writes, so a batch aborts on it; `duplicatePackage` and `importPackageUnmanaged` save each copied item through `saveMetaItem`; `migrateStoredMetadata` saves through it with `force: true`, and a stored row with nothing to convert is skipped before the save (outcome canonical/skipped), so only a row that both carries a pending conversion and sits in the refused shape meets it, and then reports `failed` with the refusal text — loud, not silent. `installPackage` stores the manifest alone (`SchemaRegistry.installPackage` takes the package's source; `POST /api/v1/packages` carries no items), so there is no item there to judge. Two write doors do not pass through `saveMetaItem` and are judged in ③: the datasource-admin service's `putDatasourceRecord`, and `rollbackMetaItem`'s `repo.restoreVersion`.

3. **The reverse direction — RIGHT.** `objectsBoundExternallyTo` reads the environment's active object rows through `readActiveOverlayRows` and parses them as the list read does (`storedOverlayEntries`, stored-row conversions replayed), then the registry's `getAllObjects()` (present on the real `SchemaRegistry`, registry.ts:4628) minus every name a stored row overlays (ADR-0029 D9: the stored row is the base layer). A datasource saved `managed` or with no `schemaMode` (the predicate's spec default) while any of them binds it with `external` is refused with one finding per object at `schemaMode`, the stored row unchanged; pinned for a stored row, a registered object, a stored overlay that dropped `external`, draft and publish mode, and the re-judge at the datasource draft's publish. Drafts are not counted, by design, and the object draft's own publish is where it is judged (pinned both ways). A read failure other than an unprovisioned store rethrows through `rethrowUnlessMetadataStoreUnprovisioned` (the shared `isMissingTableError` discriminator), so no answer is invented.

4. **The refusal shape — RIGHT, the schema gate's own.** `422` with `code: 'INVALID_METADATA'`, `issues` attached unconditionally as `MetadataIssueEntry` rows (`path` a string, `code: 'custom'`), and the message `TYPE/NAME failed spec validation: ` plus `specValidationFindings(writeFace, issues)` — the same constructor the per-type Zod gate uses a few lines above, rendered per face the same way (`meta-envelope` headline on the HTTP doors, full prose elsewhere). The issue path `external` matches #25168's parse-time refusal at the same door; the datasource half reports at `schemaMode`, the key the author changes. In `promoteDraftForPublish` the face is omitted, as its sibling `defaultRecordPageSaveRefusal` call omits it. Every refusal pin in the new test asserts code, status, path and the finding's first sentence spelled out.

5. **Nothing broader than the rule — RIGHT.** A datasource declared `schemaMode: 'external'` or `'validate-only'` is accepted on both halves (predicate returns no verdict for any `schemaMode` other than `'managed'`; pinned, including a re-save). A stack-declared datasource keeps its answer: the per-stack collector in `stack.zod.ts` is unchanged. A datasource no layer holds gets no verdict: `readMetaItem` on the active face answers `item: undefined` when the stored row, the metadata service, the artifact and `registry.getItem` all miss, so `declared` is `undefined` (pinned as a control); a degraded metadata-service read throws its own 503 before any verdict (the Acceptance note is true). The alias spellings `mode` and `schema_mode` cannot reach the raw-body read of the datasource half: `DatasourceSchema` is a `strictObject` whose `aliases` are refusal suggestions, so the schema gate refuses those keys with a prescription before this block runs. Stored rows already in the refused pair: no read, boot or load path is touched, so they load as before; the next save of either side is refused until the datasource is federated or the objects drop `external`, and the changeset says so in its Unchanged bullet and gives the fix in order. A legal object draft whose datasource turns managed before publish stays a draft (`draft|external`, pinned) with a loud 422 naming the fix.

6. **`composeStacks` — re-judged, RIGHT.** `collectComposedExternalBindingDatasourceErrors(stacks, objects)` runs in step 3b beside the two existing artifact-scoped rules, over the composed objects (after the conflict strategy) and the concatenated `datasources` of every input, with `STACK_CROSS_REFERENCE_INVALID` 422 and the per-stack finding text; pinned in both input orders, under `last` and `preserve`, for both managed shapes, plus a `strict: false` input holding the pair itself (newly refused here, as the pass's other rules do) and three controls. A name two inputs declare is judged by the later declaration (the collector keeps the last it meets), stated in the docblock. One limit the pass shares with its siblings: an input that is itself a `preserve`-composed multi-package artifact has had its top-level `objects` and `datasources` deleted in step 7, so neither this rule nor `collectArtifactCrossReferenceErrors` sees what its `packages[].body` carries — the PR's Acceptance notes name it; the changeset's "every manifest strategy, preserve included" is true of direct inputs. Note only.

7. **Public surface — RIGHT.** `data/index.ts` re-exports the module; `api-surface/data.json` and `export-origins/data.json` each gain exactly the two rows the declaration on #18549 names (`externalBindingDatasourceRefusal (function)`, `ExternalBindingDatasourceRefusal (interface)`), both resolving to `src/data/external-binding-datasource.ts`; Lint & Repo Gates (api-surface, dual-source, exported-any) success. `@objectstack/spec/data` is an `exports` subpath, and `protocol.ts` imports from it beside symbols it already took from there. No `.describe()` moved, so no generated reference moved.

8. **The docs example (`content/docs/data-modeling/external-datasources.mdx`) — TRUE.** §5's write example now binds `datasource: 'warehouse'`, and the page's own §1 declares `name: 'warehouse'` with `schemaMode: 'external'`, so the example is one the parse accepts; as written it bound `'default'`, which #25192 refuses at module load. The new §2 paragraph lists the doors correctly; one imprecision for the lane seat's prose ACCEPT: it credits `ObjectSchema.create()` with refusing a binding "on a `managed` datasource", while that door judges only the `'default'` half. Prose face, not this record's.

9. **Remainder for the lane seat's ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT`:** `scripts/engine-double-contract.pinned.json`, three rows (`delete`, `findOne`, `update`) for the new test's engine double, from `check-engine-double-contract --write`, named in the dev report's gates line; and the one-line relabel of the `lake` control in the #25192 test, whose assertions are unchanged.

### ② Semver level

- `.changeset/25211-external-binding-save-doors.md`: `'@objectstack/spec': minor` and `'@objectstack/metadata-protocol': minor` — RIGHT. The diff moves source in exactly those two packages, both published (no `private` flag, `18.0.0`); `Metadata-protocol: narrowed` is the kind (a value the save doors stored is now refused), and a kind takes at least `minor` on every package the diff moves. `@objectstack/rest` is not moved; no changeset owed there.
- `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` — RIGHT, and the correction from the claim's provisional `no (narrowing)` is the right one. `scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs` defines `yes (narrowing)` as "a diff that widens one surface and narrows another"; the value answers 「本卡放宽接受集或扩大公开面吗」 — two api-surface rows added is a public-surface expansion, so `yes` — and the arm declares the narrowing, which is BREAKING. `record-recognisers` reads the narrowing face off it and `check-adr-0087-registration` carries it as a self-test case. Line-initial in the PR body and the changeset; `Metadata-protocol: narrowed` line-initial in both.
- BREAKING banner present; FROM names the three doors as they stored; TO names each door's refusal, the draft re-judge and `force`; Unchanged names the rule, the federated controls, the no-layer case, the admin PATCH door and the stored rows; the one-line fix for an author is given in order. The `!` is on the title.
- ADR-0087 disposition: exactly one marker, `adr-0087: not-required (already-registered object-external-binding-managed-datasource-refused) …`. The id resolves at HEAD and pre-exists at base (PR #25192's D3 entry, merged `fe0ec2bb9e`); this diff amends the entry's `surface`, `replacement` and `reason` and adds no entry, so `already-registered` is the category, not `registered`. Check Changeset success.
- Semantic entry: amended rather than a second entry — RIGHT: one rule, one id, the same refused stored shape, with the entry's prose now naming `composeStacks` and both save doors; `acceptanceCriteria` unchanged. `gen:migration-registry` output is gitignored, so nothing further was owed. Note: the `REFUSED_STORED_SHAPES` detector (`refused-shapes.ts`) still resolves a named datasource only from the same stack's `datasources`, and its `surface` string still reads "a managed one the stack declares", so `os migrate meta --stored` does not list a stored object bound to a stored managed datasource; such a row surfaces only when a save or a migrate-apply meets the door. Listing-only, in ③.
- The #25168 changeset is left as stock (inherited, skipped by the gate's status rows); the new changeset names which of its sentences it narrows. Both are unreleased, so the published CHANGELOG carries them in order with the correction stated. Acceptable.
- `content/docs/releases/` untouched; `skip-changeset` not claimed.

### ③ Boundary flags

Dev report 6347635039: `open_questions: []`; no `deviations` key. Two deviations exist by #25192's own precedent and are accepted here: the branch is the thread's designated `claude/project-thread-4lefhe`, not an `issue-25211` slug (the claim names it; "The card this PR closes must claim this branch" success), and `scripts/engine-double-contract.pinned.json` sits outside the claim's file surface (mechanical `--write` output, named in the gates line). The seat may ask the dev to carry a `deviations` array next time; it does not move this verdict.

Out-of-scope finding (class b): `DatasourceAdminService.updateDatasource` via `PATCH /api/v1/datasources/NAME` — **real, and a bypass of this card's datasource half.** Read on the head: `putDatasourceRecord` (datasource-admin-plugin.ts) calls `metadata.register('datasource', …)` and `persistDatasourceRow`, which inserts or updates the `sys_metadata` row directly; `saveMetaItem` is never entered, so the record it stores is judged by `assertValidRecord` alone. `createDatasource` writes through the same seam, so the POST door can also mint a managed datasource under objects that already bind it `external` (an object saved while the name was held by no layer got no verdict, correctly). The object half is unaffected: that service writes no object. It is not this card's door — the card and the triage name the metadata-protocol save doors, the claim's surface excludes `packages/services`, and #25168's triage routed the rule away from `service-datasource` — and the PR body, the changeset's Unchanged bullet and the report all name it, so the claim here is honest. It should become a card: lane `domain:services` (the service and its routes are theirs), size S now that the predicate is exported: judge the merged record in `createDatasource` and `updateDatasource` against the objects bound to it with `external` (the service already reads `listObjects` for `countBoundObjects`), refusing with an ADR-0112 envelope through `externalBindingDatasourceRefusal`, so there is still one copy of the rule.

Acceptance notes, each answered:
- Batch publish judged one promotion at a time, in batch order — accepted; whichever half is promoted second meets the other as active and is refused before `repo.promoteDraft`, so the inconsistent pair cannot fully land; only which finding is reported depends on the order.
- Registry half reads `getAllObjects()` when present — true of the real registry (registry.ts:4628); a double without it counts stored rows only. Accepted.
- Not covered: `installPackage`'s named-datasource half — the manifest-only install carries no items (judged in ①.2), and the item-carrying copies go through `saveMetaItem`; nested `preserve` inputs — shared with the sibling artifact rules (①.6). Accepted, both named.
- Degraded metadata read surfaces as the read's own 503 — true (`readMetaItem`'s `throwMetadataServiceUnavailable`; `objectsBoundExternallyTo` rethrows all but the unprovisioned-store case). Accepted.
- #25168's changeset untouched — judged in ②. Accepted.
- Docs — judged in ①.8. Semantic entry — judged in ②.

Escalated, not blocking:
- `rollbackMetaItem` writes through `repo.restoreVersion` and asks none of the save-door refusals (not this one, nor the default-record-page, hook-body or elevated-flow siblings), so a rollback of either side to an older version can re-create the pair this card refuses. A pre-existing shape of that door, outside this card's named doors; the engine seat decides whether it is a card.
- The `REFUSED_STORED_SHAPES` detector's blind spot for a stored managed datasource (②): a `os migrate meta --stored` listing gap, spec lane, small.
- The maintainer channel the claim names (a metadata-protocol narrowing under 「协议变更直接处理，排查相关的任务，和我沟通」) is the seat's to carry at landing, together with the ADR-0015 §4.2 wording note already with the maintainer from #25168.
